name: SE-GA

paper.title: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents

construction.unit: step record ⟨screen, action, next screen⟩; experience entry ⟨trajectory, reflective summary, text key, image key⟩; rule text
construction.kept_as: steps and trajectories as recorded; an agent-written summary per trajectory
construction.processing: append every executed step; after a task the agent writes a reflective summary of the trajectory; entries are embedded (text and image)
construction.writer: the GUI agent itself for summaries; how semantic rules are produced is not described

organization.structure: three typed stores: episodic step list, semantic rules, experiential trajectories
organization.stores: M_EPI (current task), M_SEM (persistent rules), M_EXP (past trajectories)
organization.index: text embeddings for rules and intents, visual embedding for the task screen (code: text-embedding-3-small, CLIP ViT-B/32)

management.operations: append only; successful trajectories accumulate in M_EXP during inference and are later distilled into weights by MASE

retrieval.query: instruction Q; current screenshot o_t for the visual term
retrieval.candidates: episodic: last H steps; semantic: cosine(Q, rule key); experiential: λ·text + (1−λ)·visual similarity
retrieval.selection: top-K per store; only the summaries g(τ) of retrieved experiences enter the context
retrieval.budget: code defaults: H = 10 steps, 3 rules, 3 experiences, λ = 0.7; the paper gives no values

use.context: recent step records, rules and experience summaries, with the instruction and screenshot
use.reasoning: the policy VLM writes a progress check, a rationale and a history summary, then one action per step

classify.note: The episodic part is a recency window, not a search; the experiential key mixes text and image similarity. Memory contents are also used as training data (MASE).

stages.ingestion: Each executed GUI step is recorded as (observation, action, next observation) in the episodic store of the current task.
stages.construction: After a task, the trajectory is stored in experiential memory with an agent-written reflective summary, a text key and a visual key. Semantic memory holds general interaction rules; the paper does not say how they are written.
stages.organization: Three separate stores: episodic (current task), semantic (rules), experiential (past trajectories).
stages.update: Append-only: new trajectories keep accumulating during inference; nothing is merged or deleted.
stages.retrieval: Per step: the last H episodic steps; the top-K rules by cosine to the instruction; the top-K experiences by a λ-weighted mix of instruction-to-intent and screenshot-to-task similarity, keeping only their summaries.
stages.answer: The retrieved memory, instruction and screenshot go to the policy VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-7B based), which reasons and outputs one action.
stages.learning: MASE turns collected trajectories into training data: hindsight goal-shifting relabels failed trajectories with the sub-goal they reached; the policy gets grounding SFT and then GRPO with token-level ratios, an adaptive upper clip and a format/type/parameter reward.

summary: GUI agent with three memories (recent steps, general rules, past trajectories retrieved by text plus screenshot similarity) whose collected trajectories are relabelled by hindsight goal-shifting and distilled into the policy with SFT and GRPO.

The paper gives no values for H, K, λ or the encoders; the values here are the code defaults. control.construction = prompted-llm because the agent writes the reflective summary; rule creation is not described. sources.code_note: HEAD of the official repository (7 commits, 2026-05-10 to 2026-06-02; the last two only add model links). It contains the TTME memory classes with a toy example and the MASE training scripts, but no inference or evaluation code for the benchmarks.

abstract.text: SE-GA targets GUI agents that lose track of long tasks and cannot learn from their own runs. At test time it keeps three memories: the recent steps of the current task, general interaction rules, and past trajectories with reflective summaries that are retrieved by instruction and screenshot similarity. The trajectories it collects are then used to retrain the policy: failed runs are relabelled with the sub-goal they did reach, and the model goes through grounding SFT followed by a modified GRPO. With a 7B Qwen2.5-VL base, the authors report 89.0 on ScreenSpot, 75.8 success on AndroidControl-High and 39.0 on AndroidWorld.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

headline: Memory feeds the agent at each step (recent steps, rules, experience summaries) and also becomes training data for the policy.
The paper gives no window size, top-K, λ or encoders; the code defaults are H = 10, 3 rules, 3 experiences, λ = 0.7, text-embedding-3-small and CLIP ViT-B/32.
Only the ablation separates memory from training: removing TTME drops AndroidControl-High success from 73.8 to 61.4.

open_questions: The ablation removes TTME as a whole, so the separate value of episodic steps, rules and experiences is not measured; a recency window of 10 steps alone may account for much of the gain.
No run compares the same trained policy with and without experiential memory on AndroidWorld, where the paper credits both memory and self-evolution.

Baseline numbers are largely copied from another paper while SE-GA is trained on AITW, AMEX and GUIOdyssey trajectories; overlap between training sources and GUIOdyssey test episodes is not discussed.

glance.a: A step record for the current task, a rule text, or a past trajectory with an agent-written summary.
By a weighted mix of instruction-to-intent text similarity and screenshot-to-task image similarity (λ 0.7 in the code); the top 3 summaries are shown.

glance.q: Is there reranking or an LLM in retrieval?
glance.a: No. Episodic memory is a recency window; the other two are cosine top-k.
Yes, indirectly: collected trajectories are relabelled and used for SFT and GRPO (MASE).

ablation.src: paper Table 4 (7B); AC-High SR of the full model is 73.8 here but 75.8 in Table 2

discussion.takeaway: A GUI agent gains most on long, multi-step tasks when it both carries structured memory at test time and is retrained on its own relabelled trajectories.

claims.claim: State of the art among 7B GUI agents.
claims.evidence: ScreenSpot 89.0 (above UI-TARS-72B 88.4); AndroidControl-High SR 75.8; GUIOdyssey 83.9; AndroidWorld 39.0 vs UI-TARS-7B 33.0. Tables 1-3

claims.claim: TTME matters most on long-horizon tasks.
claims.evidence: Without TTME: AC-Low SR 88.6 → 83.0, AC-High SR 73.8 → 61.4. Table 4, App. C.3
Without MASE: AC-High SR 59.7, GUIOdyssey SR 60.4 (full 73.8, 83.9). Table 4
Success-only retrieval 70.0 / 72.5 vs top-k 75.8 / 83.9 (AC-High / GUIOdyssey). Table 9

limits: Retrieval cost grows as experiential memory accumulates and may slow real-time use.
Training data is limited to about 4K trajectories.
No explicit sub-goal decomposition for very long workflows; cross-platform transfer untested.
reading: Table 4 reports 73.8 for the full model on AndroidControl-High SR while Table 2 reports 75.8 for the same setting; Table 7 labels its columns AndroidControl-High and GUIOdyssey but repeats Table 4's AndroidControl-Low and -High values.

Most baseline rows are copied from another paper (App. A.5), so they may differ from SE-GA in prompts and evaluation scripts; the paper does not say where the Qwen2.5-VL, OS-Atlas, OS-Genesis and GUI-Critic-R1 numbers come from.
The paper gives no memory hyperparameters and the released code has no evaluation pipeline, so the TTME settings behind the reported numbers cannot be confirmed.
The memory described for training (Eq. 7) and the released training prompts differ: the prompts carry only a short history of up to 10 steps.
ScreenSpot is single-screen grounding, so its gain cannot come from memory; the paper attributes it to the reward design.
